text:
Marathon Petroleum stock gained nearly 3% today after climbing $25 in just four trading days, driven by a sharp reversal in oil market sentiment. Early last week, crude prices had dipped below $90 a barrel on hopes for a near-term Iran deal, but Trump administration officials have since signaled little diplomatic progress and renewed military pressure — causing Brent crude to rebound to $107 and US oil to hold firm at $99.64. Higher oil prices directly boost refiner profits, and with US refineries running at 94.5% capacity utilization, Marathon is positioned to capture more margin on each barrel processed.

The stock's recovery also reflects reduced geopolitical risk premium: as military threats persist but peace talk hopes have faded, markets appear to be pricing in a more stable (if tense) status quo rather than either a sudden breakthrough or major new escalation. This clarity has allowed energy investors to focus on the improving fundamentals — tighter oil markets and high utilization rates — rather than the binary all-or-nothing outcome that spooked sellers earlier in the week.
